title: Transactional promotion choreography with session adhesion and drain policy
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: production rollouts we see frequently fail when session-affine traffic and short-lived transactions are promoted without an ordered handoff. This PR implements a transactional promotion choreography that guarantees session-consistent promotions by combining a short-term session drain window with a traffic adhesion policy. The intent is to make model promotions atomic from the caller's perspective while enabling safe, observable, and reversible phased rollouts. Design summary: 1) Promotion transaction: a three-phase protocol (prepare -> reconcile -> commit) that records cohort state and ensures either full promotion for in-flight sessions or safe fallback. 2) Session adhesion: an adhesion policy pins existing sessions to the origin model for the duration of the drain window; new sessions can be routed to target cohort according to the normal sampling policy. 3) Drain policy: a configurable soft- and hard-drain timer plus an escape hatch that rebinds sessions to origin during failures. 4) Telemetry and safety gates: built-in SLO/metric gates (latency, error-rate, token-variance) and automatic rollback triggers. Backwards compatibility: the protocol is opt-in per rollout and defaults to legacy behavior for existing rollout specs. Migration: small schema bump to rollout CRD with optional fields (promotion_mode, adhesion_window_seconds, transactional_id). Tests: unit tests for protocol state machine, simulated multi-cohort e2e test that exercises session handoff, and load test scripts that verify no request duplication under session-affine traffic. Checklist: - [x] Implement state machine and storage hooks - [x] Add session-adhesion router integration - [x] Add telemetry and gates wiring - [x] Add e2e simulations and unit tests - [x] Add runbook and console UI for configuring adhesion/drain - [x] Perf smoke to validate latency impact - [x] Docs and changelog Notes: This description includes the core design and operational assumptions. For a short playbook see docs/runbooks/promotion_choreography.md. Linked issues: ENG-2031, ENG-2119. CI is green after flake rerun. Merge strategy: squash-merge with commit message summarizing the choreography and runbook.

release_notes: Introduce transactional promotion choreography (opt-in) with session-adhesion and drain policies. Provides safer model promotions for session-affine workloads; includes telemetry gates and automatic rollback triggers. See docs/runbooks/promotion_choreography.md for operational guidance.
operational_playbook_summary: When enabling transactional promotion: 1) start with adhesion_window_seconds=10, monitor latency and request error-rate gates for 30 minutes; 2) if gate breaches, abort prepare and fall back to origin; 3) use the console to trigger manual commit once smoke passes; 4) to rollback, issue abort transaction which rebinds sessions and drains new traffic back to origin. Emergency escape hatch: set adhesion_window_seconds=0 to immediately stop binding new sessions.
notes_for_oncall: If you see session-mismatch alerts, run /bin/promo-checker --transaction=<id> to inspect cohort state and use 'promo abort' to revert. Telemetry tags: rollout.transactional=true. Contact @maya for escalation.
